title: Listen, then invest
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Does your company listen to the people who tell it the market has changed?

I said that strategy isn't just big-picture thinking. It can be a discussion in products, administrative processes, channel strategies, geographic reach, brand identity, customer service. Our mistake is thinking it is a big conceptual umbrella when it is all of these little silos.

I called it market-needs-based positioning, I said. A lot of us say: this is my competency and what I want to do. But that is not necessarily what the market needs or what will create long-term customers for you.
I said: I think strategy is first and operational structure is second. I don't see a company making it without a solid strategy. I'm open for discussion on that one.
A student told of working for a company whose management was far away and didn't understand the market's price sensitivity, and for lack of an overall strategy they kept raising prices.

A student said: listening is the key. The strategy should be derived from the tactical responses. When you go out and do the tactical work you get a response back, and that is how you derive a rapid strategy.

I said the second step is: after they listen, does the company invest in the procedures that are essential to your strategy? It is not one investment, it is continually investing. You can talk until you are blue in the face about strategy, but does the company listen, and does it invest?
A student said that a well-known management writer has a famous line: structure supports strategy. The organization's internal structure needs to be designed to enable the execution of its strategy.
What would a customer say your company should have listened to?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what the market needs, in the market's words.
Write where that differs from what you like doing.
Write who tells you the strategy is not working.
Write what you will invest in so the strategy can be carried out.
Write how your structure supports your strategy.

check.q: What did I call positioning by what the market needs?
What did a student say a strategy should be derived from?
choices: The tactical responses you get back

check.q: What did I say a company must do after it listens?
choices: Keep investing in procedures essential to the strategy

recap: Position by what the market needs. Listen, then invest. Make structure support strategy.
